paper.title: Improved Best-of-Both-Worlds Guarantees for Multi-Armed Bandits: FTRL with General Regularizers and Multiple Optimal Arms

unmapped: Environment chooses losses arbitrarily with knowledge of the learner's algorithm; regret is pseudo-regret against best arm in expectation
settings.definition_quote: In the adversarial setting, the environment decides the loss vectors in an arbitrary way with the knowledge of the learner's algorithm.

settings.name_in_paper: MAB, stochastic setting / adversarial regime with a self-bounding constraint (Condition 1), without uniqueness
unmapped: Multiple optimal (zero-gap) arms allowed; bounds depend on |U| (number of zero-gap arms) and on D, an upper bound on E[sum_t max_{i in U} E^t[l_i^t - l_{i*}^t]] (0 in iid, <= C in corrupted)
settings.definition_quote: there exists a gap vector $\gap \in [0,1]^{K}$ and a constant $C\geq0$ such that $\Reg^T \geq \E\sbr{ \sum_{t=1}^{T} \sum_{i \in [K]} \Pr\sbr{i^t=i} \gap_i  } - C$

settings.name_in_paper: Decoupled Exploration and Exploitation MAB (DEE-MAB), adversarial setting
unmapped: Decoupled feedback: learner exploits arm i^t (suffers its loss) and observes loss of a separately chosen exploration arm j^t
settings.definition_quote: a variant of MAB where in each round $t$, the learner picks an arm $i^t$ to exploit and an arm $j^t$ to explore, and then suffers the loss $\ell^t_{i^t}$ while observing the feedback $\ell^t_{j^t}$.

unmapped: Decoupled feedback: exploitation arm i^t and observed exploration arm j^t
Multiple optimal arms allowed; bound depends on D
settings.definition_quote: The Decoupled Exploration and Exploitation MAB (DEE-MAB) problem ... the learner picks an arm $i^t$ to exploit and an arm $j^t$ to explore

algorithms.name: FTRL with log-barrier + arm-dependent learning rate (Algorithm 1, alpha=0)
FTRL with Shannon entropy + arm-dependent learning rate (Algorithm 1, alpha=1)
FTRL with beta-Tsallis entropy + arm-dependent learning rate (Algorithm 1, alpha=beta)

source.label: thm:main_log_barrier
source.quote: When using the log-barrier regularizer with $\clog = 162$, $\alpha=0$, and $\theta=\sqrt{1/\log T}$, Algorithm 1 ensures $\Reg^T = \order\rbr{\sqrt{KT\log T}}$ always

results.notes: Horizon T used in learning rate; doubling trick mentioned as alternative.

bound.expression_latex: \order\rbr{\gapcomp \log T + \sqrt{C \gapcomp \log T} +  \frac{K^2}{\sqrt{\log T}}  + K\log T + D}

symbols.G_cplx: |U|/Delta_min + sum_{i in V} 1/Delta_i, with U the zero-gap arms and V the positive-gap arms
symbols.D_bias: upper bound on E[sum_t max_{i: Delta_i=0} E^t[l_i^t - l_{i*}^t]] (0 in iid, at most C in corrupted)

extra_assumptions: no uniqueness of optimal arm required

source.label: thm:main_log_barrier
source.quote: and simultaneously the following regret bound when Condition~(1) holds: $\Reg^T = \order\rbr{\gapcomp \log T + \sqrt{C \gapcomp \log T} +  \frac{K^2}{\sqrt{\log T}}  + K\log T + D}$.

results.notes: C is the self-bounding constant, mapped to C_sb.

extra_assumptions: C_log = 162 log K, theta = sqrt(1/log T)

source.label: thm:main_shannon
source.quote: When using the Shannon entropy regularizer with $\clog = 162\log K$, $\alpha=1$, and $\theta=\sqrt{1/\log T}$, Algorithm 1 ensures $\Reg^T = \order\big(\sqrt{KT}\log T\big)$ always

symbols.D_bias: upper bound on E[sum_t max_{i: Delta_i=0} E^t[l_i^t - l_{i*}^t]]

source.label: thm:main_shannon
source.quote: and simultaneously the following regret bound under Condition~(1): $\Reg^T = \order  \Big(\gapcomp \rbr{\log T}^2 + \sqrt{C \gapcomp \rbr{\log T}^2} + K^2 \log^{3/2} T + D \Big).$

source.label: thm:main_tsallis
source.quote: For any $\beta \in (0,1)$, when using the $\beta$-Tsallis entropy regularizer with $\clog = \frac{162 \beta }{1-\beta}$, $\alpha=\beta$, and $\theta=\sqrt{(1-\beta)/\beta}$, Algorithm 1 ensures $\Reg^T = \order \Big(\sqrt{\frac{1}{\beta\rbr{1-\beta}}KT\rbr{\log T}^{\ind\cbr{\beta \neq \frac{1}{2}}} }\Big)$ always

results.notes: Proof in appendix only shows sqrt(KT log T/(beta(1-beta))); the beta=1/2 log-free case relies on remark.

bound.expression: G_cplx*log(T)/(alpha_ts*(1 - alpha_ts)) + sqrt(C_sb*G_cplx*log(T)/(alpha_ts*(1 - alpha_ts))) + D_bias + K**2*sqrt(alpha_ts)/(1 - alpha_ts)**(3/2) + alpha_ts*K*log(T)/(1 - alpha_ts)

symbols.D_bias: upper bound on E[sum_t max_{i: Delta_i=0} E^t[l_i^t - l_{i*}^t]]

source.label: thm:main_tsallis
source.quote: and simultaneously the following regret bound under Condition~(1): $\Reg^T = \order\rbr{\frac{\gapcomp \log T}{\beta\rbr{1-\beta}} + \sqrt{\frac{C\gapcomp \log T}{\beta\rbr{1-\beta}}} + D + \frac{K^2\sqrt{\beta} }{ \rbr{1-\beta}^{3/2}} + \frac{\beta K \log T}{1-\beta} }$.

extra_assumptions: C_log=0, theta=K^{1/6}, alpha=1/2, beta=2/3; exploration arm sampled with g_i proportional to p_i^{2/3}

source.label: thm:main_dee
source.quote: For the DEE-MAB problem, the algorithm described above ensures $\Reg^T = \order(\sqrt{KT})$ always

results.notes: Learning rate K^{1/6} sqrt(t) does not depend on T, so treated as anytime. Adversarial bound also previously known from Rouyer & Seldin.

symbols.D_bias: upper bound on E[sum_t max_{i: Delta_i=0} E^t[l_i^t - l_{i*}^t]]

source.label: thm:main_dee
source.quote: and simultaneously the following regret bound under Condition~(1): $\Reg^T = \order \Big(\sqrt{\sum_{i \in V} \frac{K}{\Delta_i^2}} + \sqrt{C} \cdot \rbr{\sum_{i \in V} \frac{K}{\Delta_i^2}}^{1/4} + K + D \Big)$.

results.notes: Sum over V (positive-gap arms) mapped to sum_subopt.
